text:
B: Hello! Hi, can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah. Graham.
B: Hi, Graham, I'm Akosua. Sorry, I talk a lot when I'm nervous, so just stop me. Where are you?
A: Tipton.
B: Tipton. Is that near Birmingham? Esi's dad, my daughter's dad, he's in Birmingham.
A: Near enough. Black Country.
B: Okay. I'm in Thornton Heath, South London. My daughter's nine, Esi. I saw the school photo behind you. Are they your grandchildren?
A: Yeah. Our son's two.
B: Ah, they look lovely. Do you see them a lot?
A: Sundays. Most Sundays. There's three. Our daughter's got one an' all.
B: That's nice. Sundays for us is church. My mum and me, we go in Croydon, and then we come home and I'm just shattered, honestly. Is that okay? Is that what you wanted to know?
A: Sorry?
B: Sorry, I mean, I'm just going on about myself.
A: No. It's alright.
B: Okay. Erm. What did you do for work, before?
A: Toolmaker. Then maintenance. Fixing things.
B: Oh, so you can fix anything! Esi's bike has had a flat tyre since the summer and nobody in my house knows what to do. My brother said he'd do it, and that was months ago.
A: Inner tube. Yow want a puncture kit. Or a new tube, they're cheap. Get the wheel off, find the hole in a bowl of water.
B: A bowl of water?
A: Bubbles. Where it's leaking.
B: Oh, that's clever! I'm going to try that. Okay. I'm writing it down in my head.
A: I do the grandkids' bikes. Mowers for next door.
B: You see, that's useful. I'm in HR, well, I was. I'm looking for a job right now. My skill is talking, which you can't fix a bike with.
A: Talking's useful.
B: Thank you, Graham. Are you retired then?
A: Three year.
B: Do you enjoy it?
A: Er... it's alright. Me knees are bad, so.
B: My mum's knee is the same. She was a care worker, all that lifting, and now it's playing up all the time. She wants to go back to Ghana one day, she says it's the cold here. Sorry, I'm going off again.
A: Ar. Cold doesn't help.
B: Okay, I think we're nearly finished. It was nice to meet you. Thank you for the bike tip!
A: Bowl of water. Tara.
